tests.title: Lesson and Activity week 3 pr2 Imporance of QNR in different field

questions.q: What is the main purpose of quantitative research?
c: To support decision-making and policy formulation

questions.q: What is the strength of quantitative research in generalizing research findings?
c: It can be replicated on many different populations and sub-populations
It provides precise, quantitative, numerical data
It involves data analysis which is relatively less time consuming
It can be used to obtain data that allow quantitative predictions

questions.q: What is the weakness of quantitative research in terms of data analysis?
c: It provides precise, quantitative, numerical data
It is relatively less time consuming
It involves data analysis which is relatively less time consuming
It requires extra resources to analyze the findings/results

questions.q: What is the benefit of quantitative research in psychology?
What is the purpose of standardized testing in education?
c: To provide a standardized measure of student achievement

tests.title: Lesson and Activity week 4 pr2 Types of Research Variables

questions.q: Which of the following is an example of a research variable?
c: A teacher's attitude towards a subject

questions.q: What is the role of the intervening variable in an experiment?
c: To explain causal links between variables
To observe the outcome of the experiment

questions.q: What is the dependent variable in an experiment?
c: The variable being tested and measured
The variable that is stable and unaffected
The variable that is the cause of the effect
The variable that is the outcome of the experiment

questions.q: What is the independent variable in an experiment?
c: The variable the researcher/experimenter changes or controls
The variable that is stable and unaffected
The variable that is the cause of the effect
The variable that is the outcome of the experiment

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a type of independent variable?
What is the purpose of using a control group in an experiment?
c: To test the effect of the independent variable
To observe the outcome of the experiment

questions.q: Which of the following is an example of a dependent variable?
c: A teacher's attitude towards a subject

tests.title: Lesson and Activity week 5 Traditional Vs IMRAD format

questions.q: What are the different types of Quantitative Research?
How are Quantitative Research and Qualitative Research different?
c: Quantitative Research uses numerical data and statistical methods
Qualitative Research uses non-numerical data and qualitative methods
Both types of research use a combination of data types
The difference is irrelevant to the research process

questions.q: What is the purpose of the Introduction in a research paper?
c: To state the research problem and objectives
To provide an overview of the study's scope and significance
To present the theoretical framework and conceptual framework
To provide a general framework for the research paper

questions.q: What is the main difference between the Traditional format and IMRAD format?
c: The Traditional format has a more rigid structure
The IMRAD format is more flexible and adaptable
The Traditional format is easier to replicate and compare
The IMRAD format is more effective for communicating complex research

questions.q: What is the purpose of the Literature Review in a research paper?
c: To provide an overview of the study's scope and significance
To present the theoretical framework and conceptual framework
To review and synthesize relevant literature on the topic
To provide a general framework for the research paper
